Q: Can't execute jupyter notebook in terminal: "execution_count": null A: 
As a workaround, I have created a script `clean_notebook.py` that removes the faulty lines:

clean_notebook.py

import json import pathlib import sys from copy import deepcopy

def clean_cell(cell): cell = deepcopy(cell) if cell.get("cell_type") == "code" and "execution_count" in cell: del cell["execution_count"] # Supprime complètement la clé return cell

def main(nb_path): nb_path = pathlib.Path(nb_path) data = json.loads(nb_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) data["cells"] = [clean_cell(c) for c in data["cells"]] nb_path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1), encoding="utf-8") print(f"✔️ Nettoyé et validé : {nb_path}")

if name == "main": if len(sys.argv) != 2: print("Usage: python clean_notebook.py <notebook.ipynb>") sys.exit(1) main(sys.argv[1])


run  `py clean_notebook.py Untitled.ipynb` before your execution.

Q: How to execute command inside vim? A:

Since Vim 8.1, it's possible to open an embedded, interactive terminal with the :terminal (short: :term) command. You can run any kind of shell commands in this terminal window and yank and put to and fro other buffers.
See :help terminal for the documentation of all the features.

This is especially useful if you want to issue more complex commands, need to monitor a long-running command or want to run variations of the same command.
For a one-off command or to filter text through an external command, the methods presented in Jonathan Leffler's answer are to be preferred.

For sake of completeness, before :terminal was added, there was the :shell command which runs a terminal in full screen mode. On systems that support it, you can also suspend Vim using Ctrl-Z to go to the calling shell and run commands there (fg to go back to Vim).

Q: Is there a mechanism to loop x times in ES6 (ECMAScript 6) without mutable variables? A:

Since the introduction of iterator helpers in ECMAScript 2025, you can do:

Array(10).keys().forEach((_, i) => {
    console.log(i * 10);
});

This does not populate an array, and so the memory for it is constant, no matter what the length is for it. The forEachmethod here is not the Array method, but the Iterator method.

Note that if you just need a string repeated you can use String.prototype.repeat.

console.log("0".repeat(10))
// 0000000000

Q: I'm having trouble with understanding memory space of GWLP_USERDATA A:

Q1. cbWndExtra allocates extra bytes that are accessible via positive indexes in (Get|Set)WindowLong[Ptr]. OS-provided fields are accessible via negative indexes. This includes GWLP_USERDATA (-21).
